answer.rationale: Objective is minimize TCO without increasing delivery risk. Line is at 94% with no buffer and the primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew, so a primary-vendor change or a deferral is a supply-cliff risk; stockout cost would dominate any unit-price gain. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is unlikely to clear the 18% mandate in time. add_second_source as the single action would not replace the expiring primary. memory_c1 is the directly applicable stability record for renewal; memory_c2 is the competing low-cost switch claim and must be checked before treating a 14-day cutover as low-risk. memory_c5 (month-to-month deferral) does not transfer to a non-auto-renewing contract and is not relied on. Renewal forgoes the low-cost quote but is the only one-decision path that does not raise delivery risk; TCO here includes line-down exposure.
